title: Dashboard sprint cookbook: metric rename proposals and migration notes
content:
Purpose
------
Quick working guide for the upcoming dashboard sprint where we rename a set of runtime and routing metrics, consolidate tag conventions, and update 3 high-traffic dashboards. This doc captures rationale, rename mappings, cost impact estimates, canary steps, and rollback notes. Meant to be a "single source of truth" while the migration is in-flight.

Scope and constraints
---------------------
- Affects metrics emitted by inference proxies + runtime reducers only (no agent-side telemetry changes this sprint).
- Goal: rename & normalize metric names/tags for consistency with the new metric taxonomy (see linked artifact ENGOBS-412).
- Low-risk rollout: must not break dashboards for oncall or automated alerting. Alerts should continue to fire during migration.
- Query cost budget: dashboards must remain within the monthly Prometheus/TSDB query budget; where a rename increases cardinality, we must add rate limiting or sampling.

High-level migration plan
-------------------------
1) Prepare mapping table and update instrumentation layer to emit both old_name and new_name for 2 weeks (dual-write shim).
2) Update dashboards to include both names (left: old metric, right: new metric) and mark widgets with "migration:dual" tag.
3) Run canary: enable dual-write in staging, then in 5% of prod traffic for 24h; validate parity with query diffs and trace anchors.
4) Flip dashboards to prefer new metric after 72h of stable parity and no SLI regressions.
5) After 30 days, remove old emission and clean up queries.

Rename / normalization proposals (examples)
------------------------------------------
- Runtime latency metrics (previous messy names -> proposed canonical)
  - runtime.infer.latency_p50_ms -> runtime.inference.latency_p50_ms
  - runtime.infer.latency_p95_ms -> runtime.inference.latency_p95_ms
  - runtime.infer.latency_p99_ms -> runtime.inference.latency_p99_ms
- Token economics / cost metrics
  - cost.tokens.per_request -> economics.tokens_per_request
  - request.cpu_gpu_seconds -> economics.compute_seconds_per_request
- Cache / KV metrics
  - kv.cache_hits -> cache.kv.hits_total
  - kv.cache_misses -> cache.kv.misses_total

Tag normalization examples
-------------------------
- Tenant tag: "tenant_id" -> "org_id" (canonical across stack)
- Model: use "model.repo" + "model.version" instead of a single freeform "model_name" tag to reduce cardinality and enable model-level rollups.
- Region: "region" stays; prefer full region name (us-west1) not AZ-level.

PromQL / query examples to support dual-read dashboards
------------------------------------------------------
- P50 latency (dual):
  - old: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(runtime_infer_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, org_id))
  - new: histogram_quantile(0.5, sum(rate(runtime_inference_latency_bucket[5m])) by (le, org_id))
- Combined widget (show both series):
  - vector("old:${old_query}") and vector("new:${new_query}") — annotate legend with "(old)" and "(new)"

Trace anchor changes and drift checks
-----------------------------------
- Trace span name changes: old span "infer_request" -> new span "runtime.inference.request". For parity checks, we will keep both span names emitted by the runtime for dual-write period.
- Drift check: sample 1 per 1000 requests and compare span duration distribution between old/new spans. If median differs > 5% for 24h, pause rollout.

Dashboard widget mapping (migration checklist)
--------------------------------------------
- Dashboard: "Runtime Overview"
  - Widget A (latency histogram): swap to new metric but keep old visible with faded color; tag widget: migration-dual
  - Widget B (top models by p95): update query to use model.repo + model.version grouping
  - Widget C (alerting panel): keep old metric as primary until alerts confirmed to work with new metric for 48h
- Dashboard: "KV Cache Health"
  - Replace kv.cache_hits with cache.kv.hits_total; add dimension-by-org panel to ensure no high-cardinality explosion

Query cost estimation heuristic
-----------------------------
- For each renamed metric, compute estimated increase in cardinality = (#new_tag_variants) / (#old_tag_variants). If > 3x, mark metric as "cost-risk" and restrict high-cardinality rollups to sampled dashboards only.
- Example: kv cache hit previously had tag set {env,service} (6 combos). New tags add org_id (expected ~200 orgs) -> cardinality ~1200 -> 200x increase. Action: only emit org_id for aggregated metric (cache.kv.hits_total:org_rollup=true) and emit detailed per-org metric behind a sampling gate.

Instrumentation checklist for engineers
--------------------------------------
- [ ] Implement dual-write shim in runtime library (feature flag runtime.metric_dual_write=true)
- [ ] Add ability to redact org_id for any env where cardinality > threshold (config-driven)
- [ ] Add unit tests ensuring both metrics increment on request path
- [ ] Add integration job to compare old/new time series for parity (daily job)

Canary test plan (prod)
----------------------
- Canary cohort: 5% traffic routed through canary runtime variant; enable dual-write
- Validation gates:
  - Parity: time series difference < 1% for p50/p95/p99 across 24h window
  - Trace consistency: sampled spans parity check OK
  - Dashboard stability: no spike in query latency or increased panels timeouts
  - Alerting: verify one test alert fires for both old and new metric copies

Rollback plan
-------------
- If parity fails or query cost spikes occur, flip runtime.metric_dual_write=false in canary; dashboards still show old metrics as primary. Postmortem within 48h.
- If issue originates from dashboard queries (e.g., accidental high-cardinality joins), revert dashboard changes and mark problem widget as "disabled" in dashboard-annotations.

Cleanup and follow-up
---------------------
- After 30 days of stable operation: deprecate old metric in exporters and remove dual-write code path.
- Submit housekeeping PR to remove old queries from dashboards and add a migration note in README with the date of removal.
- Add permanent SLI to track metric emission counts for renamed metrics (emit meter.metric_migration.events with labels {name,action}).

Open questions / outstanding decisions
------------------------------------
- Do we standardize on model.repo vs org-owned model identifier? (affects tag normalization; pending product decision)
- Sampling rate for per-org detailed metrics: default 1/1000? need perf SRE input.
- Do we want to add a retention tier for high-cardinality metrics (30 days vs 90)? Finance input required.

Next steps (this week)
----------------------
- Marcus: draft dual-write shim PR and include feature flag toggle (due 2025-02-21)
- Elena: update 3 dashboards with dual-read widgets and annotate (due 2025-02-25)
- Samir: run initial cardinality analysis and produce cost-risk list (due 2025-02-22)
- Ops: schedule canary rollout window (2025-02-28 02:00 UTC)

Notes to reviewers
------------------
- This is intentionally written as a sprint cookbook — please comment inline with any blockers or missing rollback paths. We expect lots of small follow-ups.
- Keeping both metrics for at least 30 days minimizes alert fatigue and gives SRE teams time to tune thresholds.
